papers.title: LongStraw: Long-Context RL Beyond 2M Tokens under a Fixed GPU Budget

summary.tldr: LongStraw enables million-token RL post-training under fixed GPU budgets by optimizing execution for long contexts, addressing the gap between inference and training context lengths.
key_points: LongStraw evaluates shared prompts without autograd and retains only model-specific state for later tokens.
It replays short response branches one at a time, reducing the live training graph at the cost of additional replay time.
LongStraw completes grouped Qwen scoring and response backward at 2.1M positions for groups of 2 and 8 on eight H20 GPUs, with a stress test reaching 4.46M positions.
It validates end-to-end execution for a 2.1M-token prompt across 78 layers of GLM-5.2 on 32 H20 GPUs.
summary.why_it_matters: This allows AI agents to process and learn from significantly longer trajectories, improving their ability to handle complex, multi-step tasks.

papers.title: VideoChat3: Fully Open Video MLLM for Efficient and Generalist Video Understanding

summary.tldr: VideoChat3 is a fully open, efficient, and generalist video-centric MLLM that uses Inflated 3D Vision Transformer (I3D-ViT) and Adaptive Frame Resolution for streaming video perception, trained on three diverse datasets.
key_points: VideoChat3 introduces Inflated 3D Vision Transformer (I3D-ViT) for efficient spatiotemporal representation.
Adaptive Frame Resolution for Streaming Video Perception reduces processing cost during training and inference.
A scalable video data synthesis pipeline curates three datasets: VideoChat3-Academic2M, VideoChat3-LV116K, and VideoChat3-OL617K.
VideoChat3 achieves broad generalization and computational efficiency with 4B parameters.
VideoChat3 surpasses prior open-source models on general, long-form, and streaming benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: VideoChat3 provides a fully open-source, efficient, and generalist solution for video understanding, addressing limitations in current models regarding generalization, computational demands, and reproducibility.

papers.title: SEED: Self-Evolving On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: SEED introduces a self-evolving on-policy distillation framework that converts completed trajectories into hindsight skills, generating dense token-level supervision for agentic reinforcement learning.
key_points: SEED fine-tunes the policy to analyze completed trajectories and generate natural-language skills (reusable workflows, decisive observations, failure-avoidance rules).
The current policy collects trajectories and extracts hindsight skills, allowing policy updates to improve both decision-making and skill analysis.
SEED re-scores sampled actions under ordinary and skill-augmented contexts, converting the skill-induced probability shift into a dense token-level on-policy distillation signal.
This distillation signal is jointly optimized with outcome-based RL, maintaining alignment with the current trajectory distribution.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves performance and sample efficiency in agentic tasks by addressing the supervision gap between episode-level outcomes and token-level policy learning.

papers.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration

summary.tldr: SearchOS introduces a multi-agent framework for robust open-domain information seeking by externalizing search progress into explicit, shared state and employing pipeline-parallel scheduling and a Search Tool Middleware Harness.
key_points: SearchOS formulates open-domain information seeking as relational schema completion with grounded citations, where agents discover entities, populate attributes, and anchor values to source evidence.
Search-Oriented Context Management (SOCM) externalizes evolving state into a Frontier Task, an Evidence Graph, a Coverage Map, and Failure Memory to track task progress.
SearchOS utilizes a pipeline-parallel scheduling mechanism to overlap sub-agent execution and continuously refill freed slots with tasks targeting unresolved coverage gaps.

A Search Tool Middleware Harness intercepts model/tool interactions to record grounded evidence, react to stalls/budget exhaustion, and provides a hierarchical skill system to avoid repeating failed search patterns.
SearchOS outperforms single- and multi-agent baselines on WideSearch and GISA benchmarks across all metrics.
summary.why_it_matters: This system improves the efficiency and completeness of information-seeking agents by preventing repetitive search loops and optimizing resource utilization.

papers.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong

summary.tldr: BadWAM introduces World-Action Drift Attacks, a new class of adversarial attacks that use small visual perturbations to desynchronize a WAM's imagined future from its executed actions.
key_points: BadWAM defines two attack types: action-only adversarial attacks for maximum disruption and imagination-preserving adversarial attacks for stealth.
Action-only attacks directly drive the WAM toward task-failing actions, reducing success rates from 96.5% to 43.1%.
Imagination-preserving attacks induce harmful action shifts while maintaining the model's predicted future close to its clean imagination.
Future-preserving regularization can maintain strong attack performance in imagination-preserving attacks while reducing future imagination drift.
summary.why_it_matters: This research exposes a critical vulnerability in World-Action Models, demonstrating that their perceived robustness and safety through coupled action generation and world prediction can be fragile under adversarial conditions.

papers.title: KeyFrame-Compass: Towards Comprehensive Evaluation of Keyframe-Conditioned Video Generation

summary.tldr: KeyFrame-Compass is the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating keyframe-conditioned video generation, revealing limitations in current models regarding keyframe execution and video quality.
key_points: KeyFrame-Compass includes 386 curated samples across three application domains, two video structures, two prompt granularities, two conditioning formats, and four keyframe densities.
The automated evaluation framework measures keyframe execution using six metrics: presence, fidelity, temporal ordering, localization, persistence, and uniqueness.
Overall video quality is assessed via evidence-grounded MLLM judgments augmented with specialized perception models.
Experiments on nine video generation systems show a trade-off between faithful keyframe execution and natural video synthesis, with performance degrading under denser keyframe constraints.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark identifies fundamental limitations in current keyframe-conditioned video generation models, guiding future research and development towards more robust systems.

papers.title: MultiRef-Compass: Towards Comprehensive Evaluation of Multi-Reference-to-Audio-Video Generation

summary.tldr: MultiRef-Compass is a new benchmark for multi-reference-to-audio-video (MR2AV) generation, addressing the gap in evaluating models that jointly reason over multiple references for coherent audio-visual content.
key_points: MultiRef-Compass comprises 350 curated samples from a scalable asset-composition pipeline, covering multi-view subject preservation, multi-entity binding, and human-object-scene composition.
The benchmark defines an evaluation protocol with four dimensions (Basic Quality, Reference Consistency, Audio-Visual Consistency, Instruction Following) and 14 sub-metrics.
It integrates automatic metrics with a rejudging-enhanced MLLM-as-a-Judge framework for scalable and auditable evaluation.
Experiments on eight MR2AV systems reveal significant room for improvement across evaluation dimensions.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark provides a standardized method to assess and advance the capabilities of MR2AV generation models, which are crucial for creating complex, multi-faceted audio-visual content.

papers.title: Concurrent Image Understanding and Generation: Self-Correcting Coupled Markov Jump Processes

summary.tldr: SC-CMJP introduces a framework for concurrent image understanding and generation using coupled Markov Jump Processes, enabling cross-modal self-correction and remasking within Masked Diffusion Models.
key_points: SC-CMJP allows one modality's transition rates to be functionals of the other modality's confidence score, weighted by cross-modal attention.
A remasking jump retracts commitments when cross-modal evidence contradicts them, addressing MDMs' inability to remask.
CO_2Jump is a novel training-free single-pass sampler for joint multimodal generation, implemented within the SC-CMJP framework.
Three large-scale joint multimodal generation corpora (JEdit-1M, JMaze-200K, JNono-200K) are created for training and evaluation.
CO_2Jump achieves best joint performance in image understanding/editing and visual reasoning (maze/nonogram solving), with performance scaling monotonically with denoising steps.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables more robust and coherent joint multimodal generation by allowing real-time self-correction and cross-modal consistency enforcement.

papers.title: UniVR: Thinking in Visual Space for Unified Visual Reasoning

summary.tldr: UniVR introduces VR-GRPO, a reinforcement learning paradigm, to learn complex reasoning, physical dynamics, and long-term planning directly from pure visual demonstrations, achieving up to 25% improvement on the new VR-X benchmark.
key_points: UniVR is the first system to simultaneously learn complex reasoning, fine-grained physical dynamics, and long-term planning from pure visual demonstrations.

UniVR utilizes VR-GRPO, a reinforcement learning paradigm with global and step-level rewards, to enforce logical coherence and physical consistency without task-specific heuristics or image-text pairs.
VR-X is a new large-scale benchmark, curated from 16 diverse sources, designed to assess long-horizon manipulation, spatial puzzles, and physical reasoning under a purely visual protocol.
UniVR achieves up to a 25% improvement on the VR-X benchmark and enhances performance on various multimodal understanding benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: This research demonstrates the potential for advanced visual reasoning capabilities to be learned directly from visual data, reducing reliance on explicit textual or task-specific guidance.

papers.title: RxBrain: Embodied Cognition Foundation Model with Joint Language-Visual Reasoning and Imagination

summary.tldr: Hy-Embodied-RxBrain is an embodied cognition foundation model using a multimodal Mixture-of-Transformers for joint language-visual reasoning and imagination in planning sequences.
key_points: RxBrain represents embodied plans in a single planning sequence, integrating language for abstract structure (task decomposition, constraints, temporal order) and visual imagination for grounding through world state prediction and joint subgoal planning.
The model utilizes a unified multimodal Mixture-of-Transformers architecture for understanding and generation across language, image, and video modalities.

Training involves an automatic pipeline converting embodied videos into joint text-visual planning supervision by decomposing videos into planning steps and aligning them with visual state transitions.
RxBrain-Bench is introduced to evaluate models' ability to represent embodied plans via joint textual and visual components.

RxBrain demonstrates embodied understanding and generation, producing plans with coupled textual reasoning, world state prediction, and joint subgoal planning, and extends to continuous robot action generation with promising real-robot performance.
summary.why_it_matters: This model provides a step towards foundation models for embodied cognition by enabling robots to connect high-level task reasoning with physical states through joint language-visual planning.

papers.title: Spectral Rewiring for Exploration, Purification, and Model Merging

summary.tldr: Subspace-Aligned Rewiring (SAR) is a post-hoc editing method that extracts reasoning-effective components from RL updates in large language models, preserving performance while reducing interference.
key_points: SAR retains the spectral core of RL updates, removing orthogonal components to preserve reasoning gains and filter performance-suppressing or interference-amplifying directions.
SAR extracts compact reasoning cores using approximately 0.58% of total parameters, preserving over 99% of post-training performance.
SAR improves high-k exploration in mathematical reasoning and enhances agentic coding performance on six of seven open benchmarks.
SAR purifies mixed-domain training updates, releasing suppressed coding capability while maintaining math reasoning and instruction following.
SAR enables model merging across experts, achieving cross-domain generalization superior to previous merging baselines and single-domain experts.
summary.why_it_matters: SAR offers a training-free mechanism to improve reasoning and multi-domain performance in large language models by extracting reasoning-effective updates from parameter geometry.

papers.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies

summary.tldr: RoboTTT scales visuomotor context for robot policies to 8K timesteps, enabling new capabilities and significant performance gains without increased inference latency.
key_points: RoboTTT scales visuomotor context to 8K timesteps, three orders of magnitude beyond prior state-of-the-art, without growing inference latency.
It integrates Test-Time Training into robot foundation models, using fast weights updated by gradient descent during training and inference to compress histories.
The training recipe combines sequence action forcing with truncated backpropagation through time to scale context length.
RoboTTT improves overall performance by 87% over single-step context baselines and completes a five-minute, ten-stage assembly task, which baselines fail to do.
Pretraining with 8K-timestep context outperforms 1K-timestep context by 62%, indicating context length as a new scaling axis.
summary.why_it_matters: This advancement enables robots to perform more complex, long-horizon tasks, learn from single demonstrations, and adapt to perturbations in real-time.

papers.title: Video = World + Event Stream

summary.tldr: Wan-Streamer v0.3 reframes video as a persistent "world" plus a dynamic "event stream" for a general pretraining task, enabling real-time audio-visual interaction.
key_points: Wan-Streamer v0.3 models video as a "world" (persistent context like environment, subjects, acoustics) and an "event stream" (temporal changes like scene shifts, behavior, speech).
The pretraining task involves predicting how the "world" changes and responds in real-time given the "world" and incoming input.
The model supports real-time full-duplex audio-visual interaction, mapping multimodal user input to language-form speech and behavior actions.
It maintains v0.2 operating points: 640x368 video at 25 FPS, 160 ms streaming unit, ~200 ms model-side latency, and ~550 ms total interaction latency with a 350 ms network budget.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework provides a general approach for real-time video understanding and interaction, applicable to various downstream tasks requiring responsive AI.

papers.title: Demystifying On-Policy Distillation: Roles, Pathologies, and Regulations

summary.tldr: On-policy distillation (OPD) acts as an exploration catalyst, guiding students via token-level signals, but is susceptible to Student-Teacher Mismatch and Length Exploitation pathologies, which can be mitigated by advantage clipping and log-scale compression.
key_points: OPD's primary role is an exploration catalyst, steering students with dense token-level guidance without expanding capability ceiling.
OPD effectiveness is entirely dependent on the quality of its guiding signal, with prompt diversity being more critical than per-problem sampling numbers.

Two pathologies are identified: Student-Teacher Mismatch (large teacher-student distributional gap misaligns guiding signal) and Length Exploitation (aggregated token-level objective creates length-dependent shortcuts).
Lightweight signal regulations, advantage clipping and log-scale compression, are proposed to alleviate length exploitation and ensure faithful signal guidance.
Experiments across seven benchmarks show these regulations enable effective distillation, outperforming OPD variants and RLVR baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding and regulating OPD signal quality is crucial for effective LLM post-training, preventing exploration pathologies and improving distillation outcomes.

papers.title: WanSong v1.0 Technical Report

summary.tldr: WanSong is a pure diffusion-based model for generating high-fidelity, multilingual songs up to 5 minutes with dual stems (vocals and background music) in a single run, offering faster inference via step-distillation.
key_points: WanSong is a pure diffusion-based model, diverging from autoregressive (AR) and cascaded multi-stage pipelines.
It directly generates high-fidelity, multilingual songs up to 5 minutes in a single run.
The model outputs dual stems (vocals and background music) simultaneously.
Its diffusion framework enables faster inference through step-distillation and supports efficient fine-tuning for editing tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach addresses challenges in efficient generation, high-fidelity long-form audio, and controllability for commercial-grade song production.

papers.title: Bayesian Repetition Penalty: A Principled Adjacent-Conditional Framework for Reversing Attention Collapse in Autoregressive Language Models

summary.tldr: A new Bayesian repetition penalty framework uses adjacent-conditional probability to correct anomalous confidence in autoregressive language models, reversing attention collapse without modifying training pipelines.
key_points: The framework penalizes or compensates anomalous confidence by comparing a token's observed frequency against its corpus prior using an adjacent-conditional probability construction.
The penalty ratio $R=f(m,n,p)/f(np,n,p)$ is self-normalizing and provides a closed-form logit offset with zero approximation error.
The correction is applied as a frozen output-layer bias via exponential moving average, isolated from the loss gradient.
Experimental validation on a 1.5B-parameter model reduced 2-gram repetition from 0.073 to near 0 while preserving generation quality.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a non-intrusive way to repair language models suffering from repetitive generation patterns, even after they have collapsed.

papers.title: CRAFT: Clustering Rubrics to Diagnose Weak LLM Capabilities and Generate Targeted Fine-Tuning Data

summary.tldr: CRAFT converts rubric-based evaluation datasets into model-specific diagnoses of weak capabilities by clustering grading criteria, enabling targeted supervised finetuning data generation.
key_points: CRAFT treats each grading criterion in a rubric-based evaluation as a capability probe.
It extracts capability descriptions from prompt-rubric pairs, clusters them into a hierarchical capability tree, and scores the target model at each node.
CRAFT dynamically selects low-performing nodes across tree levels to identify failures at the clearest granularity.
The method directs targeted supervised finetuning data generation based on selected weak capabilities.
CRAFT achieved the strongest average performance in the finance domain for all four tested models and in the legal domain for three of four models compared to baseline methods.
summary.why_it_matters: Diagnosing model weaknesses at the rubric criterion level provides a clearer understanding of model limitations and leads to measurably improved models after targeted finetuning.

papers.title: Loop the Loopies!

summary.tldr: The Loopie series introduces two Mixture-of-Experts models (20B/2B active and 6B/0.6B active parameters) that overcome the historical challenge of looped Transformers, outperforming vanilla Transformer baselines with equivalent compute.
key_points: Loopie series includes two MoE models: a 20B-parameter model with 2B active parameters and a 6B-parameter model with 0.6B active parameters.
Loopie models address the challenge where increasing parameter count by N typically outperforms looping a model N times for an N times increase in pre-training compute.
Ablation studies, including comparisons with a 30B-A3B model, demonstrate Loopie's substantial outperformance over vanilla Transformer baselines given the same compute budget.
Loopie achieves frontier-level reasoning performance through a novel post-training method.
summary.why_it_matters: This work demonstrates a method to improve the efficiency and performance of looped Transformer architectures, potentially leading to more capable models within given computational constraints.

papers.title: Monkey King Bang: A Unified Scientific Multimodal Foundation Model

summary.tldr: MKB is a unified scientific multimodal foundation model for understanding and generation across six scientific branches, utilizing a shared Transformer backbone and modality-tailored components.
key_points: MKB covers six scientific branches: DNA, RNA, proteins, small molecules, earth science, and medical images.
The model supports native outputs including biological sequences, molecular strings, meteorological fields, and segmentation masks.
Training involves a two-stage curriculum: modality-specific alignment with a frozen backbone, then consolidation with a language backbone using mixed scientific and general corpora.
MKB achieves competitive scientific understanding and high-fidelity native outputs, while largely retaining the general capabilities of its Qwen3-VL backbone.
summary.why_it_matters: This paradigm offers a foundation for future cross-domain scientific multimodal exploration, enabling joint understanding, reasoning, and generation across diverse scientific domains.

papers.title: Chronofy: A Temporal-Logical Decay Architecture for Information Validity in Time-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary.tldr: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems retrieve and integrate external knowledge to ground large language model (LLM) outputs. However, current RAG architectures treat all retrieved facts as equally valid regardles

papers.title: PagedWeight: Efficient MoE LLM Serving with Dynamic Quality-Aware Weight Quantization

summary.tldr: PagedWeight is a novel management method for MoE LLM serving that dynamically quantizes MoE model weights at runtime, balancing expert-weight precision with KV cache sizes to improve efficiency and accuracy.
key_points: PagedWeight dynamically quantizes MoE model weights at runtime to manage the tension between GPU memory requirements for weights and growing KV cache in KV-cache-intensive serving scenarios.
The method achieves FP16-equivalent accuracy with up to 72.0% GPU memory savings and a 1.94x throughput improvement.
PagedWeight improves quality over existing quantization methods by up to 39.3% at a similar memory budget, with a maximum 4.1% throughput loss.
It navigates the tradeoff between model task accuracy, memory consumption, and throughput/latency in MoE serving.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach significantly enhances the efficiency and quality of MoE LLM serving by optimizing memory usage and throughput while maintaining accuracy.

papers.title: BayesPO: Bayesian Prompt Optimization via Parallel-Tempered Gradient-Guided Discrete MCMC

summary.tldr: BayesPO introduces Bayesian posterior sampling for prompt optimization, using gradient-guided discrete MCMC with parallel tempering to explore prompt token space.
key_points: Prompt optimization is framed as Bayesian posterior sampling, combining a task likelihood term (explaining input-output examples) and an LLM prior (favoring fluent instructions).
The framework uses an energy-based posterior sampling problem, where gradients guide discrete Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) proposals over vocabulary tokens.
BayesPO employs a Metropolis-Hastings corrected Gibbs-with-Langevin (GwL) proposal and integrates parallel tempering for global exploration of LLM-induced energy landscapes.
Experiments with Qwen2.5 models show post-optimizing APE prompts on 24 instruction-induction subtasks improved average accuracy from 60.04% to 63.23%.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a principled, probabilistic approach to prompt optimization, potentially improving LLM performance on various tasks.

papers.title: Induction in Both Directions: A Mechanistic Analysis of In-Context Learning in Masked Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: This work mechanistically analyzes in-context learning in masked diffusion language models (DLMs), revealing a bidirectional induction circuit that utilizes both past and future context, unlike autoregressive models.
key_points: DLMs learn a bidirectional induction circuit where previous-token and next-token heads write local context into the residual stream.
Induction heads in DLMs find and copy answers from matching source positions, with the circuit being direction-symmetric.
DLMs do not outperform AR models in induction when only left context is visible, but show stronger induction with bidirectional context access.
DLMs implicitly compute and use the global fraction of masked tokens as a timestep, despite lacking explicit timestep embeddings.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding DLM induction mechanisms can inform the development of more effective and context-aware language generation models.

papers.title: An MLIR-Based Compilation Method for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: This paper introduces an MLIR-based compilation method for LLMs, utilizing TopOp and TpuOp dialects to address model import and efficient autoregressive inference on AI accelerators.
key_points: The method uses two MLIR dialects: TopOp for framework/chip-independent model semantics and TpuOp for chip-specific decisions like quantization and memory layout.
Models are lowered from TopOp to TpuOp layer by layer, generating a deployable binary.
Transformer layers are split into prefill, prefill_kv, and decode stages for static compilation to optimize prompt-parallel and per-token generation.
The approach is implemented in TPU-MLIR and LLM-TPU, supporting Qwen, Llama, InternVL, and MiniCPM-V models, with GPTQ, AWQ, and AutoRound quantization.
summary.why_it_matters: This compilation method facilitates efficient deployment of large language models on specialized AI accelerators by streamlining model representation and optimizing autoregressive inference.

papers.title: Adaptive Multi-Step Lookahead Decoding for Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: AdaLook is an adaptive multi-step lookahead decoding framework for diffusion language models that dynamically determines rollout depth and enables branch expansion to improve accuracy-efficiency trade-offs.
key_points: AdaLook dynamically determines whether to continue lookahead rollout based on candidate-score variance.
The framework enables branch expansion when intermediate rollout states require additional exploration.
This adaptive design avoids unnecessary deep rollout while allowing re-triggering lookahead from informative intermediate states.
AdaLook improves the accuracy-decoding steps trade-off compared to existing one-step lookahead decoding methods for diffusion language models.
summary.why_it_matters: AdaLook offers a more efficient and accurate decoding method for diffusion language models, potentially accelerating parallel text generation.

security.title: Microsoft at Black Hat USA 2026: Defending trust in the age of AI and supply chain attacks

summary.tldr: Microsoft Security at Black Hat USA 2026 will focus on defending against AI and supply chain attacks, highlighting new services and intelligence on npm attacks.
key_points: David Weston's keynote, "The End of Rare: Defending When Offense Is Cheap," on August 5, 2026, will address defense strategies against increasingly accessible offensive capabilities.

Aarti Borkar and Tanmay Ganacharya's session, "Poisoned at the Source: Inside the Hunt for Supply Chain Attacks," on August 5, 2026, will detail Microsoft Threat Intelligence's hunting methods for supply chain attacks, including ongoing npm attacks.
Microsoft will showcase Microsoft Defender Experts Threat Intelligence and Microsoft Defender Experts MDR, now with third-party and multicloud coverage, at booth #2144.
Threat actors are targeting trusted software, services, identities, developer workflows, and AI systems to abuse trust paths and scale impact.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding and defending against the abuse of trusted systems and AI is critical as offensive capabilities become more automated and scalable for threat actors.

infra.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin Maximizes Intelligence per Dollar for Post-Training Workloads — a Key Metric for Agentic AI

summary.tldr: NVIDIA introduces "intelligence per dollar" as a key metric for agentic AI, emphasizing continuous post-training for models that adapt to dynamic environments, distinct from traditional cost per token for inference.
key_points: Agentic AI requires continuous post-training to adapt to shifting environments, emerging edge cases, and changing tools, unlike generative models responding to static prompts.
Post-training builds intelligence through reinforcement learning (RL) techniques, involving forward passes (attempts), scoring, and backward passes (weight updates) across millions of iterations.
NVIDIA NeMo open libraries, including NeMo Gym for training environments and NeMo RL for distributed post-training, provide infrastructure for scalable post-training.
The NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a 550-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, achieved 71.7% on the SWE-bench coding benchmark using a disclosed post-training recipe on NeMo RL.
summary.why_it_matters: This shift in focus to continuous post-training and the "intelligence per dollar" metric is crucial for developing and evaluating agentic AI systems that can operate effectively in real-world, dynamic conditions.

summary.tldr: Google DeepMind introduces Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber, a new lightweight cybersecurity model designed to identify and remediate vulnerabilities.
key_points: Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber is a lightweight model.
Its primary function is to find cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
It is also designed to patch identified vulnerabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: This model offers a new tool for automated cybersecurity defense by both detecting and fixing security flaws.

vendors.title: A scorecard for the AI age

summary.tldr: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar introduces an AI scorecard to measure ROI using metrics like useful work, cost per successful task, dependability, and return on compute.
key_points: The scorecard measures ROI through useful work.
It evaluates cost per successful task.
Dependability is a key metric.
Return on compute is included in the assessment.
summary.why_it_matters: This scorecard provides a structured approach for organizations to quantify the value and efficiency of their AI investments.
